reason: 'Leaf blade ... base slightly contracted, without distinct petiole' means the leaf has no real stalk. 'Petiole absent' reads this correctly; 'distinct' only softens it.

target: add the alternative 'yellowish red' (an orange-red or yellowish-red colour value)
fix: In a list of colour alternatives, every alternative must be kept. A first alternative that is a modified colour ('yellowish red') was dropped instead of being mapped or flagged.
reason: The source gives three alternatives: yellowish red, red or dark red. The annotation keeps only red and dark red, so it leaves out a colour the flora allows.
'Lip ... subovate in outline' is the orchid lip with an approximately ovate 2-D shape.
'Flowers yellow to pale green' is a colour range on the flower. The purple markings belong to a separate statement about the lip.
'Leaflets ... acute or acuminate at the apex' gives the leaflet's apex sharpness as two alternatives. Both values are right.

fix: Read 'X with membranous margins' as the margin being membranous, not the whole part. Move the quality to the margin of the part (here the tepal margin) or fill the position slot with 'margin'.

A trichotomous inflorescence branches in threes. 'Tripartite' (synonym trifurcate) is a fair existing term for this.

'Calyx lobes ... more or less ciliate on the margins' means the sepals are approximately ciliate. Ciliate already means fringed at the margin.
In 'Plants 0.8-3 × 0.5-1.3 dm' the first number range is the height. 0.8-3 dm converts to 8-30 cm. The second range (the width) is not part of this annotation.

'Rose' as a colour means pink.
'Peduncles terminal, purplish' means the peduncle is approximately purple.

target: obovate (PATO_0001936), with the base cuneate as a separate annotation
fix: In botany, 'cuneate-X' (cuneate-obovate, cuneate-oblong) means X with a wedge-shaped base. Cuneate describes a base shape, not an outline, so it should not be read as one end of a range between two outlines.
reason: The sepals are obovate and taper wedge-like to the base. They are not 'somewhere between cuneate and obovate'.

target: leaf lamina vein (PO_0020138), the lateral (secondary) veins of the leaflet
fix: In Flora Malesiana and similar Meliaceae descriptions, 'costae ... on each side' means the lateral veins. PO 'costa' (PO_0030072) is the single midrib, mainly of mosses. Map 'costae' with 'on each side' to the lateral veins.
reason: A leaflet has one midrib, so 12-14 'on each side' can only mean the secondary veins.
The plant is hermaphroditic or possibly andromonoecious. Both values are taken as alternatives.

fix: Counts given under a 'Female flowers:' or 'Male flowers:' heading must carry that flower sex in the whole/state slot.

target: leaf lamina absent, with the whole set to the basal leaf sheaths (leaf sheath PO_0020104) of the culm
fix: Read 'bladeless sheath(s)' as the sheath lacking a blade (absence inside the sheath leaf), not as the plant lacking leaf blades. Follow the 2026-11-13 rule 'bladeless' (C350).
reason: Only the purple-brown sheaths at the base of the culm have no blade; the leaves themselves have blades. Without the whole slot, the annotation says the plant has no leaf blades.

fix: Map 'glaucous' (with a whitish or bluish waxy bloom) to PATO glaucous, never to a green colour value. The earlier 'pruinose' rule maps there too.
